extracted.intended_audience: examiners at International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities (PCT); patent applicants and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and finalizing the PCT written opinion and international preliminary examination report, including what to include in Boxes I–VIII, how to cite documents, language and timing rules, and how to handle exclusions, unity, clarity/support and applicant responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority documentation and indication of priority validity
rubrics_metrics.description: If waiting to obtain the priority document and/or the translation an appropriate comment should be made under the heading 'Additional observations, if necessary:' in Box No. II. If a copy of the priority document and/or the translation is not available because of non-compliance by the applicant with Rule 17.1 ... any written opinion ... may be established as if the priority had not been claimed and this is indicated in the report. Where the right to priority is invalid, item 2 of Box No. II ... must be completed. 'Additional observations' in item 3 of Box No. II relate to Priority considerations only and not to clarity, descriptive support, defects or any other consideration relevant to Box No. VIII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reasons for which a priority claim was considered invalid, or indicate that the priority claim had been checked and was considered valid; place remarks under Box II 'Additional observations' only for priority matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-establishment of opinion on novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability (Box III)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part explains why an opinion as regards novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability may not have been established for some or all subject matter of the international application (e.g., excluded subject matter, clarity/support defects). The first two check boxes of Box No. III are used to indicate the extent to which no opinion has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reasons mirror those for not establishing an international search, the written opinion can refer to the international search report or the declaration under Article 17(2)(a). Use Box III checkboxes to indicate the specific reason(s) for non-establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter under Rule 67.1
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some or all claims are not examined for novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability because they contain excluded subject matter, this observation is indicated in the third check box of Box No. III of the written opinion or examination report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of excluded matter include mathematical theories, plant or animal varieties and methods for treatment of the human or animal body (see Rules 43bis.1(b) and 67.1). Refer to Chapter 9 for details. If exclusion affects only some claims, indicate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity or support preventing formation of meaningful opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description, the claims, or the drawings are so unclear, or the claims are so inadequately supported by the description that no meaningful opinion can be formed on novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability, the examination may be restricted to claims or parts of claims that are sufficiently clear and supported to enable an opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the appropriate check box(es) in Box No. III and include observations on lack of clarity/support to explain the limitation of examination. Issues of clarity and descriptive support should, as appropriate, be raised separately at Box No. VIII.

rubrics_metrics.name: No international search made for some or all claims (Article 33(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the International Searching Authority has not established an international search report and instead issued a declaration under Article 17 (relating to excluded subject matter, clarity, lack of unity, etc.), the questions of novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability cannot be addressed and this is noted using the sixth check box of Box No. III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even where Article 34 amendments may have overcome earlier considerations. Note the limitation in Box III and give details in the Supplemental Box if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listings compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A failure to furnish a nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listing complying with the standard provided for in Annex C of the Administrative Instructions and in an accepted language may preclude any meaningful preliminary examination from being carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a meaningful search or examination to the extent possible; if some or all claims cannot be examined for this reason, note the reasons in the final check boxes of Box No. III and provide details in the Supplemental Box if necessary. See Chapters 15 and 18 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention observations and status indications (Box IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where unity of invention is lacking, this observation must be included in the first written opinion and, if still applicable, in subsequent opinions and the report. The opinion/report must indicate whether claims have been restricted, additional fees paid (with or without protest and with or without protest fee), or whether the applicant has neither restricted nor paid additional fees, and whether the examiner decided not to issue an invitation to restrict or pay additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which parts of the international application the opinion/report was established on, in view of findings on unity and any restrictions or additional fees paid. See also procedures for Invitations to Pay Additional Fees or to Restrict (Forms PCT/ISA/206, PCT/IPEA/405).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees paid under protest — annexing protest text and decision
rubrics_metrics.description: In Chapter II where additional fees are paid under protest, the text of the protest, together with the decision thereon, is annexed to the international preliminary examination report if the applicant has so requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the detailed procedures for annexing protests (see paragraph 10.80) and analogous Chapter I guidance where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned statement on novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability (Box V)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement as to whether the claims appear to satisfy the criteria of novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness) and industrial applicability is made in item 1 of Box No. V for each claim to be examined (YES or NO). Each such statement must be accompanied by relevant citations, explanations and observations in item 2 of Box No. V. A statement on all three criteria should be made, and the examiner should always cite documents believed to support any negative statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations must follow WIPO Standard ST.14. Explanations should clearly indicate, with reference to the cited documents, the reasons supporting the conclusions and identify particularly relevant passages (page/column/lines). For patent documents in another language, indicate corresponding part of an English family member if available. For non-written disclosures, describe the most relevant elements and give spatial/temporal references (e.g., timestamps). See Chapters 12–14 for further guidance on each consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating details for cited documents (Box VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each published application or patent referred to in the report, the examiner provides the date of publication, its filing date, and its claimed priority date (if any). If a relevant document refers to a non-written disclosure published on or after the relevant date, indicate the kind of non-written disclosure, the date on which the non-written public disclosure occurred, and the date on which the document was made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report may also indicate that, in the opinion of the Authority, the priority date of such published application or patent is not valid. See Administrative Instructions Sections 507 and relevant search-report paragraphs for manner of indicating special categories and claim relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting defects in form or contents of the international application (Box VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in the opinion of the examiner, defects exist in the form or contents of the international application (for example, failure to comply with requirements specified in Rules 5 to 11), the examiner includes this opinion in Box No. VII of the written opinion and/or examination report and indicates the reasons therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific reasons and, where appropriate, refer to paragraphs 17.09, 17.13 and 17.14 for further instruction on stating defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations on clarity and support (Box VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are significant and pertinent issues as to the clarity of the claims, the description and the drawings, or whether the claims are fully supported by the description, observations should be made in Box No. VIII. The examiner should list relevant claim numbers and indicate reasons for lack of clarity and/or support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to include observations based on their significance for further processing. Observations need not be included where likely amendments to overcome other objections would also resolve clarity/support issues; but where a positive statement on patentability for all claims is given, raise significant clarity/support matters. Cross-reference paragraphs 5.31–5.58 and 17.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalization requirements for the international preliminary examination report
rubrics_metrics.description: When finalizing the report, the Authority indicates the date the demand was submitted, the date the report was completed and the name and address of the International Preliminary Examining Authority. Every written opinion and report indicates the name of an authorized officer and of the International Authority responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete these administrative items either when including other data or at completion. Ensure authorized officer and Authority names appear on every opinion/report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of the written opinion and report
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion and the international preliminary examination report, together with its annexes, are established in the language of publication, or, if the examination is carried out on the basis of a translation, in the language of that translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applications filed in Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Korean, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian or Spanish are published in that language; applications filed in other languages are published in the language of a translation into one of these languages. See Rules 48.3 and 70.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of objection — stating the deficient part and PCT requirement not met
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of objection, the first written opinion should indicate the part of the international application which is deficient and the requirement of the PCT which is not met either by referring to specific Articles or Rules, or by other clear explanation; it should also give the reason for any objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit and cite the specific Article/Rule or provide a clear explanation so the applicant can understand and respond; where cited art demonstrates lack of novelty/inventive step and unity problems exist, consider inviting payment of additional fees if time allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting the opinion to be maximally useful for later stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive matter in the written opinion should normally be set out first. The opinion should be drafted to facilitate further international preliminary examination of the application should it be amended and to avoid extensive re-reading in case additional written opinions are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not obliged, the examiner should try to indicate amendments which would avoid a negative statement in the international preliminary examination report if a demand is filed. Use standardized clauses where appropriate but adapt as needed to fit context; standardized clauses are recommended to facilitate preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to correct or amend and time limits for reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion of the International Searching Authority includes notification that if the applicant demands international preliminary examination he is invited to file observations, correct formal deficiencies and submit amendments before the expiration of the time limit for filing the demand. Any written opinion established by the International Preliminary Examining Authority must fix a time limit for reply that is reasonable under the circumstances (normally two months, not shorter than one month, and at least two months after the international search report was transmitted; should not be more than three months after the opinion date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply to the invitation may cause the international preliminary examination report to be established with a negative determination in relation to certain claims. Set time limits carefully and ensure applicant is properly notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances for partial or no written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be cases when the Authority is not required to perform an international preliminary examination covering the whole application, or it is more efficient to defer some matters. These include: only inventions which have been searched need be subject to international preliminary examination; subject matter on which the Authority is not required to carry out examination; claims lack unity; fundamental objections (e.g., clear lack of novelty) or where amendments add matter beyond the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the scope limitation in the opinion and use the appropriate Box III/IV checkboxes or explanations. See Rule 66.1(e) and Article 34(4)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with major/fundamental objections first
rubrics_metrics.description: If fundamental objections arise (including introduced by amendment), it may be more appropriate to deal with these objections before making a detailed examination; e.g., if claims need recasting, avoid raising subsidiary clarity objections which will be moot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the first written opinion stage seek to make the maximum impact to provide a useful international preliminary report on patentability and to bring proceedings to a conclusion without undue delay to meet time limits if examination is demanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of documents not in a working language — evidence and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report may cite a document not in a working language because the examiner has evidence or strong suspicion that it is relevant. The examiner may cite the document on similar evidence in the first written opinion; an abstract or corresponding document in a working language will also be cited if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant disputes the relevance and gives specific reasons, reconsider and, if justified, obtain a translation (or the relevant part) and consider sending a copy of the translation to the applicant in a further written opinion or by informal communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considering additional documents located by the examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Although international preliminary examination is principally based on the international search report (and any supplementary report), the examiner should not be deterred from looking for relevant documents he personally knows or suspects exist if they can be located in a short time; such documents are considered on the same footing as those cited in the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat additional located documents like cited documents and cite them with the same detail and reasoning in Box V/VI as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account third-party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the International Bureau transmits a third party observation in time to be taken into account, any prior art referred to in the observation should be considered as if referred to in the international search report, provided a copy or immediate availability exists. The examiner is not required to comment on a document in a third party observation unless he considers it appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may, if useful, state in Box V that third party observations submitted on specified dates have been taken into account in preparing the opinion on novelty and inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies between description and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Serious inconsistencies between claims and description as filed should be objected to. However, where claims may require substantial amendment, the examiner might invite the applicant to amend the description to conform with the final form of the amended claims to expedite issuance of the report (if a demand is filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid putting the applicant to unnecessary expense if claims will likely change again. Use this procedure cautiously to help expedite processing without imposing undue burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommending amendments — scope and manner
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should not suggest amendments merely because they may improve wording; what matters is clarity. The examiner should try to indicate amendments that would avoid a negative statement if examination is demanded, but it is not the examiner's duty to draft amendments to meet an objection — drafting is the applicant's responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suggesting an amendment, make clear it is for the applicant's assistance and that other forms will be considered; suggested forms should follow Rule 66.8. Do not be pedantic; focus on meaning rather than wording improvements alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of applicant's responses to the written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: If issues such as clarity, support, or defects have not been suitably resolved by the applicant within the prescribed time limit, the examiner may indicate unresolved issues and the reasons in the report. If the applicant submits arguments in response, the examiner should comment on the applicant's relevant arguments in the written opinion of the IPEA and/or the international preliminary examination report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate applicant arguments and amendments; where responses do not overcome objections, identify unresolved issues and explain reasons to aid further processing or potential Chapter II actions.
